messages:
maria: Hey 👋 can someone run a quick SKU comparison for the new kernel build? Need A100 vs H100 vs L40S numbers for an autoregressive workload (bs=8, seq=2048, kvcache enabled). Focus on p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU memory usage, and tokens/s. Not super urgent but would like results before EOD if possible.

devon: On it. Do you want FP16 + q4 runs? Also confirm: continuous batching (20ms) or static batches?

maria: FP16 + q4 (if quant available). Use continuous batching set to 20ms. Include throughput (tokens/s) and a short note if you see tail spikes.

sofia: I can run A100 + L40S. H100 access is limited here—@cheng can you grab H100?

cheng: I can take H100. Heads up: kernel v2.3.1 changed fused-attention path; might affect tail latency. I'll run nvprof + flamegraph for any spikes. :mag:

devon: Running bench command locally now:
```
./bench_runner --model ./models/35b --seq 2048 --bs 8 --kvcache --batching continuous --batching-delay-ms 20 --precision fp16 --latency_pctl 50,95,99 --mem --quant q4
```
I'll post raw numbers when done.

perf-bot: Scheduled bench job #8732 on a100-40gb at 2026-03-17T14:12:16Z (runner: a100-40gb-3, ticket: infra-1221)

devon: Quick results (A100, fp16, q4 fallback succeeded):
- p50: 1.05s  p95: 1.62s  p99: 2.30s
- GPU mem (peak): 19.6 GB
- throughput: 3.8k tokens/s
(Raw logs: /tmp/bench-8732/a100.log)

cheng: H100 (same config) - initial run shows improvement on average but tail behavior odd:
- p50: 0.82s  p95: 1.12s  p99: 1.65s
- GPU mem (peak): 20.2 GB
- throughput: 5.1k tokens/s
Notes: with kernel v2.3.1 fused-attn enabled I see periodic ~+200-400ms spikes at p99. nvprof traces show a jittered kernel launch pattern around attention_fused_v2.

sofia: L40S (fp16, q4):
- p50: 1.12s  p95: 1.85s  p99: 2.60s
- GPU mem (peak): 22.1 GB
- throughput: 3.5k tokens/s
Observations: L40S memory higher due to different allocator defaults; CPU->GPU copy patterns slightly different which explains extra tail.

maria: Thanks — do we have a baseline from v2.2.9 to compare? Any obvious regressions?

devon: I ran a quick diff vs baseline v2.2.9 on a100/h100: H100 p99 is ~+12% slower vs baseline when fused-attention is enabled. If I set env var `USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=0` the p99 drops back to baseline (~-2%). So looks like fused path in v2.3.1 causes tail spikes on H100.

cheng: Confirmed with nvprof: kernel timings show a non-uniform distribution; small but recurring stalls when attention_fused_v2 hits a specific codepath. Attaching snippet from flamegraph (trimmed):
```
attention_fused_v2 #############
kernel_launch_wait  ##
memory_copy_async ######
other_kernel  ###
```
I'll open an issue with perf traces and tag @kernel-team.

jake: I can add a perf CI canary that runs a 3-minute continuous batching scenario to detect p99 regressions. What guardrail do we want? p99 + X% relative to pinned baseline?

maria: Let's use p99 +8% as the alert threshold for H100. If tripped, CI should fail the build and open a slack thread to eng-runtime and kernel-team.

jake: Sounds good. I'll PR the job and add the threshold. Will link back here when done.

devon: For the issue/PR, use this quick repro (helps reproduce fused path spikes):
```bash
USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=1 ./bench_runner --model ./models/35b --seq 2048 --bs 8 --kvcache --batching continuous --batching-delay-ms 20 --precision fp16
```
Flip to `USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=0` to confirm regression disappears.

maria: Perfect. Please paste raw logs & PR/issue links here when created. If kernel-team needs extra traces I can run extended nvprof. Thanks all! :thumbsup:
